## From a timing decision to a control function

- Chapter 11 chooses one intervention start time.
- Here $u(t)$ is a bounded, function-valued intervention.
- Classification: deterministic, continuous-time, continuous-state,
  population-level, ODE-constrained.

Use normalized states $S,I,C$ with $S(0)=0.99$, $I(0)=0.01$ and $C(0)=0$.
The horizon is $T=20$, $0\leq u\leq0.5$, and $\int_0^T u(t)\,dt\leq2$.

::: {.notes}
The support points used by the transcription are numerical degrees of freedom;
they do not make the mathematical control discrete.
:::

## Controlled SIR and objective

$$
\dot S=-(1-u)\beta cSI,\quad
\dot I=(1-u)\beta cSI-\gamma I,\quad
\dot C=(1-u)\beta cSI.
$$

$$
\min_u C(T)+10^{-3}\int_0^T u(t)^2dt
\quad\text{s.t.}\quad
0\le u(t)\le u_{\max},\quad \int_0^T u(t)dt\le B.
$$

The identity $C(t)=S(0)-S(t)$ is a structural validation.

## Current InfiniteOpt formulation

```{julia}
using CairoMakie, InfiniteOpt, Ipopt
T, βc, γ, umax, B = 20.0, 0.5, 0.25, 0.5, 2.0
model = InfiniteModel(Ipopt.Optimizer)
set_optimizer_attribute(model, "print_level", 0)
@infinite_parameter(model, t in [0.0, T], num_supports=15,
                    derivative_method=OrthogonalCollocation(2))
@variable(model, S >= 0, Infinite(t), start=0.99)
@variable(model, I >= 0, Infinite(t), start=0.01)
@variable(model, C >= 0, Infinite(t), start=0.0)
@variable(model, 0 <= u <= umax, Infinite(t), start=0.0)
@constraint(model, S(0.0) == 0.99); @constraint(model, I(0.0) == 0.01)
@constraint(model, C(0.0) == 0.0)
@constraint(model, deriv(S,t) == -(1-u)*βc*S*I)
@constraint(model, deriv(I,t) == (1-u)*βc*S*I - γ*I)
@constraint(model, deriv(C,t) == (1-u)*βc*S*I)
@constraint(model, integral(u,t) <= B)
@objective(model, Min, C(T) + 1e-3*integral(u^2,t))
constant_over_collocation(u,t)
optimize!(model)
```

::: {.notes}
This is the supported InfiniteOpt 0.6 path in the root environment. Ipopt
returns a local solution to the collocated nonlinear program.
:::

## Read the transcription and plot it

```{julia}
#| fig-cap: "Collocated SIR trajectory and the optimized bounded intervention over time."
ts = supports(t)
Ŝ, Î, Ĉ, û = value.(S), value.(I), value.(C), value.(u)
fig = Figure(size=(850, 350))
ax1 = Axis(fig[1,1], xlabel="time", ylabel="fraction")
lines!(ax1, ts, Ŝ, label="S"); lines!(ax1, ts, Î, label="I")
lines!(ax1, ts, Ĉ, label="C"); axislegend(ax1)
ax2 = Axis(fig[1,2], xlabel="time", ylabel="u(t)")
stairs!(ax2, ts, û); hlines!(ax2, [umax], linestyle=:dash)
fig
```

Check bounds, nonnegativity, and the incidence identity before interpretation.
Refining supports is the relevant numerical convergence experiment.

## What SDDP can—and cannot—do here

The historical nonlinear SIR script is **not** a current SDDP model:
`LinearPolicyGraph` requires affine constraints and objectives. Products such as
$uSI$ and exponential infection updates violate that restriction.

- Defer nonlinear stochastic SIR control.
- A defensible SDDP exercise first builds an explicit linear inventory-like
  approximation and reports what epidemiological nonlinearities were discarded.
- Do not present that proxy as an exact solution of the controlled SIR problem.

See the [InfiniteOpt quick start](https://infiniteopt.github.io/InfiniteOpt.jl/stable/tutorials/quick_start/),
[InfiniteOpt docs](https://infiniteopt.github.io/InfiniteOpt.jl/stable/), and
[SDDP restrictions](https://sddp.dev/stable/).

::: {.notes}
The limitation is a modeling boundary, not a missing macro. Use a supported
transcription for the deterministic nonlinear problem and a different method
when stochastic nonlinear dynamics are essential.
:::
